title: Deck-based lateral navigation and workspace lanes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Proposal for a railless, deck-based navigation model that surfaces major console areas as horizontally arranged 'decks' and introduces workspace lanes to reduce context switching friction. Each deck groups related routes (e.g., Models, Deployments, Observability) with lightweight in-deck routing. Workspaces become first-class lanes that can be pinned, collapsed to initials, or layered as parallel strips to facilitate fast cross-workspace comparisons (cost, traffic, rollout status). The design focuses on clarity for engineers and product teams who manage multiple projects and need to track rollout state and cost signals without losing routing semantics or breaking deep links.
acceptance_criteria: Primary navigation implemented as horizontally scrollable decks with clear deck titles and a stable URL for each deck state
Workspace lanes can be pinned and reordered; pin state persists per-user and is reflected in the URL fragment for shareability
Dashboard, Rollouts, and Cost views are addressable within a deck with a predictable breadcrumb and deep-link behavior
Compact collapsed deck mode reduces footprint to icons+initials and preserves keyboard-only access to all routes
Prototype validates 80% of usability tasks in moderated testing (switch workspace, open rollout, compare cost across two workspaces) within 2 interactions
design_notes: Move away from a single vertical rail to reduce cognitive distance between related areas — decks group horizontally instead of nesting vertically
Introduce 'lanes' as a lightweight orthogonal layer: lanes are workspace contexts, decks are functional areas
Routing: maintain canonical routes for every deep state (e.g., /workspace/:id/deck/:deckId/route/:routeId) so links and analytics remain stable
Keyboard-first access: quick-jump (CMD+K) augmented with lane toggles and deck previews
Accessibility: ensure ARIA role landmarks for deck containers and visible focus rings in collapsed mode
review_feedback: Marcel Reyes (PM): Liked the lateral decks for reducing deep-scan time; concerned about discoverability of less-used routes — suggest adding an overflow 'More' deck
Sana Iqbal (Engineering): Highlighted implementation risk for persisted pin state across browsers; recommends server-side storage behind feature flag
Evan Cho (Research): Prototype testing indicated users expected a vertical grouping by default; recommend an onboarding tooltip and an optional 'classic rail' toggle
decisions: Adopt deck + lane model as default in the experimental feature flag for Beta customers
Persist pinned lanes in user settings (server-side) to support multi-device consistency
Add an overflow 'More' deck for low-usage routes instead of increasing deck density
Keep canonical, shareable URLs for every in-deck route to preserve analytics and links
risks_mitigations: Risk: Users may not discover routes hidden in collapsed decks — Mitigation: add progressive hinting and onboarding overlay
Risk: Increased complexity for routing and deep-link mapping — Mitigation: router migration guide and automated redirect rules from old rail paths
Risk: Performance regressions on initial render for customers with 50+ workspaces — Mitigation: lazy-render lanes and virtualize deck list
next_steps: Finalize Figma components and annotate interaction specs (3 days)
Hand off to ENG with a prioritized implementation plan and feature-flag gating (PM+ENG sync)
Coordinate moderated usability sessions with 8 power-users focusing on cost comparison and rollout inspection flows
Create telemetry plan: deck impressions, lane pin/unpin events, deep-link usage
